paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two example selection methods, ST-ES and Random, in relation to the number of in-context examples, measured by minADE20. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linear, ranges from 0 to 15, and is marked at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "minADE20," is linear, ranges from 15.00 to 17.00, and is marked at intervals of 0.5. The blue line, representing ST-ES, starts at approximately 17.25 on the y-axis when the number of examples is 0, then sharply decreases to around 15.00 at 2 examples, and continues to gradually decrease to about 14.75 at 8 examples, remaining relatively stable with minor fluctuations until 15 examples. The orange line, representing Random, begins at around 16.75 on the y-axis when the number of examples is 0, decreases slightly to approximately 16.50 at 2 examples, and remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations around this value until 15 examples, with a slight dip to around 16.40 at 10 examples before returning to around 16.50.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods, ST-ES and Random, in terms of minADE20 as the number of in-context examples varies. The x-axis represents the "Number of Examples" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 15 with a tick interval of 5. The y-axis is labeled "minADE20" and has a linear scale, spanning from 15.00 to 17.00 with a tick interval of 0.5. The ST-ES method is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style, while the Random method is depicted by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style. The ST-ES line starts at approximately 17.25 on the y-axis when the number of examples is 0 and decreases sharply to around 15.00 at 2 examples, then continues to decrease gradually to about 14.80 at 6 examples, after which it remains relatively stable, ending at approximately 14.80 at 15 examples. The Random line begins at around 16.80 when the number of examples is 0, decreases slightly to about 16.50 at 2 examples, and then remains relatively stable, ending at approximately 16.50 at 15 examples.
